extracted.intended_audience: open-source investigators, investigative journalists, and researchers using OSINT methods
extracted.subtask_description: A curated directory of guides, handbooks, video series, protocols, and toolkits for conducting open-source investigations (geolocation, satellite imagery, verification, ethics, handling sensitive content, etc.). Meant to help practitioners learn methods and standards for OSINT and investigative reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bellingcat Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: The resources section on the website includes a large amount of guides on a variety of topics, including geolocation, using satellite imagery, and so on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bellingcat Tech Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Youtube series that helps open source researchers learn how to use tools and technical research methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification Handbook (various editions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Several editions which are available in various languages: Verification Handbook, Verification Handbook for Investigative Reporting, Verification Handbook for Disinformation and Media Manipulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Investigative Journalism Network Resource Center
rubrics_metrics.description: Guides on various journalism-related topics including open source investigations. Relevant sections are amongst others: Investigative Techniques and Reporting Tools & Tips.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quiztime
rubrics_metrics.description: Solve geolocation challenges to improve your open source research skills. By Julia Bayer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordings from the International Journalism Festival
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings of most sessions from the International Journalism Festival in Perugia are available online. This list shows panels that are of interest for open source researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Berkeley Protocol on Digital Open Source Investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Document outlining terms, guidelines, and standards for conducting open source research for human rights investigations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic reading list
rubrics_metrics.description: List of scholarly readings on open source research and methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: OSINT at Home
rubrics_metrics.description: YouTube Series from Ben Strick on how to do open source research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordings from Bellingfest
rubrics_metrics.description: Recordings of various open source research related talks from Bellingfest (10 years of Bellingcat).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposing the Invisible
rubrics_metrics.description: Resources for investigators by Tactical Tech.

rubrics_metrics.name: Online course: Open Source Investigations for Human Rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Two videos, 90 minutes each. Offered by Amnesty International. They also have a page with a limited number of guides.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video as Evidence Field Guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Offered by Witness. Particularly relevant for open source researchers: Ethical Guidelines: using eyewitness videos in human rights reporting and advocacy (pdf) and: using eyewitness videos in human rights reporting and advocacy (pdf).

rubrics_metrics.name: Open-Source Practitioner’s Guide to the Murad Code - Pilot Version
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides standards and practices for how to deal with information related to systematic and conflict-related sexual violence (SCRSV) during open source investigations. Offered by the Institute for International Criminal Investigations and the Human Rights Center at the University of California, Berkeley School of Law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bellingcat - SGBV guide
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognising Sexual and Gender-Based Violence as an Open Source Researcher.

rubrics_metrics.name: INHOPE hotline
rubrics_metrics.description: Report potential child sexual abuse material (CSAM) online.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to Maintain Mental Hygiene as an Open Source Researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: Guide with practical steps and browser extensions to limit exposure to graphic content online.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting your Moral Compass: A Workbook for Applied Ethics in OSINT
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided by the Stanley Center for Peace and Security.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Replaybook: A field guide to the climate and information crisis
rubrics_metrics.description: Insights from 30 organisations and practitioners on the climate and information crisis (includes a contribution from Bellingcat founder Eliot Higgins).
